memory_candidates.content: When building an efq-free birelational canonical model with a TWO-CLAUSE canonicalR (box clause + diamond-image clause, needed for MValid/Cd/Idb-bearing systems), box_refuting_theory/dia_refuting_theory (SegmentLindenbaum.lean) alone are NOT sufficient -- they only establish the box clause (or the seeded membership), not the diamond-image clause under witness extension. The 'far' clause requires a Lindenbaum-PAIR (set-)exclusion lemma (excluding an entire target SET of formulas via a disjunction argument, not just one formula). IK's existing prime_set_exclusion/modal_set_exclusion is structurally efq-dependent (its disjunction-property proof needs bigOr_append_left, whose empty-list base case is bot->phi) and CANNOT be reused efq-free. Resolution: reimplement the Lindenbaum-pair machinery over NONEMPTY lists represented as an explicit (head, tail) pair, with iterated disjunction/conjunction (bigOr1/bigAnd1) terminating at the head instead of at bot -- every step IK discharged via efq at the empty-list base case is discharged instead via OrI1/OrI2/the identity implication (x->x via implyK+implyS). This pattern (task 495, MinCanonicalModel.lean) is reusable for any future efq-free two-clause canonicalR construction, e.g. task 501's CT/CS4/CS5 if built atop MK rather than IK.

When adding a new Modal/Metalogic subtree that reuses shapes from an existing sibling development (e.g. IK's CanonicalModel.lean), watch for NAME COLLISIONS in the shared Cslib.Logic.Modal namespace: canonicalR, canonicalVal, canonicalVal_upward_closed are already taken by Intuitionistic/CanonicalModel.lean. A per-file `lake build` will NOT catch this (it only surfaces when the whole project is built and both files' declarations land in the same namespace via Cslib.lean's transitive imports) -- always run a full `lake build` (not just the scoped module build) before declaring a new modal metalogic file complete, and prefix new declarations with a scope-specific prefix (e.g. `min`) from the start rather than after the fact.
